Sympy exact-polynomial expansion independently gave det(F)-2rho*x(1-x)*(x-eps^2)*(x-1/2)=0 identically. The original primary theorem supplies positive semidefiniteness on K_epsilon and existence of finite-degree certificates. On a fixed I strictly inside [1/2,1], every generator weight has uniform positive lower bound, so each SOS matrix coefficient is bounded by the bounded target. Bernstein–Walsh/Cauchy from I to a disk about 0 gives uniform C_R R^d control on first and second jets with any R>3+2sqrt2. At x=0 positivity of all unweighted blocks forces first column zero and S11 prime=0; the global PSD determinant inequality bounds S12 prime by sqrt(S11 second derivative * S22(0)/2). Differentiate off-diagonal identity: unit-size rho derivative must be at most const*(sqrt(eps*R^d)+eps^2*R^d), a contradiction below degree coefficient 1/log R. Sending R down proves liminf, not degree equality, and finite rational tests do not prove it.
